h1: CCAT Practice Test & Quiz — Instant Answers While You Practice
subhead: Take a free practice quiz or point your phone at any Criteria Cognitive Aptitude Test question for the answer plus a fast explanation of the logic — build speed under the real time pressure.
metaTitle: CCAT Practice Test & Quiz: Instant Answers | Cambo
metaDescription: Free CCAT (Criteria Cognitive Aptitude Test) quiz and practice questions with instant, explained answers. Math, verbal, and spatial reasoning — build speed for the real 15-minute test.
whyItWorks: The CCAT gives you 50 questions in 15 minutes across math, verbal, and spatial reasoning — the hard part usually isn't the difficulty, it's the clock. Cambo answers a practice question instantly so you can see the pattern, understand why it's right, and move to the next one without losing your pace.

sampleQuestions.q: All project managers at the firm are PMP-certified. Lexi is a project manager at the firm. Which conclusion follows?
options: Some project managers at the firm are not PMP-certified
There is not enough information to draw a conclusion
sampleQuestions.a: Lexi is PMP-certified — this is a straightforward syllogism: every member of the group has the certification, Lexi is a member of the group, so Lexi has it too.

sampleQuestions.q: A worker can complete a task alone in 8 hours. Working together with a second worker, the task takes 3 hours. How long would it take the second worker alone?
sampleQuestions.a: 4.8 hours — the combined rate is 1/3 of the job per hour; subtracting the first worker's rate of 1/8 leaves 5/24 per hour for the second worker, or 24/5 = 4.8 hours.

sampleQuestions.q: A rectangular garden is 12 feet long and 8 feet wide. What is its area?
sampleQuestions.a: 96 square feet — area of a rectangle is length × width, so 12 × 8 = 96.

sampleQuestions.q: BOOK is to READ as FORK is to ___?
sampleQuestions.a: EAT — a book is the object used for the action of reading, just as a fork is the tool used for the action of eating; the analogy matches object-to-its-primary-use.

sampleQuestions.q: A train travels 300 miles at a constant speed and takes 5 hours. If it needs to cover 480 miles at the same speed, how long will it take?
sampleQuestions.a: 8 hours — the speed is 300 ÷ 5 = 60 mph, so 480 ÷ 60 = 8 hours.

sampleQuestions.q: If each shape in a row rotates 90 degrees clockwise from the one before it, what does the next shape in the sequence look like?
options: The prior shape rotated a further 90 degrees clockwise
The first shape in the row, repeating the cycle
The prior shape rotated 90 degrees counter-clockwise
sampleQuestions.a: The prior shape rotated a further 90 degrees clockwise — CCAT spatial questions reward tracking the single consistent transformation rule across the row rather than guessing.

faqs.a: The Criteria Cognitive Aptitude Test is a 50-question, 15-minute pre-employment assessment measuring math, verbal, and spatial reasoning under time pressure. Employers administer it through Criteria Corp during hiring.
Most employers look for a score in the top half for the role, but the exact cutoff varies by employer and position — some technical or analytical roles set a higher bar.
That depends on the employer administering it — some allow a retake after a waiting period, others don't. Check with the company you're applying to.

faqs.q: Is Cambo affiliated with Criteria Corp?
faqs.a: No. Cambo is an independent study tool and isn't produced, endorsed, or affiliated with Criteria Corp or the CCAT.

faqs.q: What kinds of questions are on the CCAT?
faqs.a: A mix of math word problems, verbal reasoning and vocabulary, and spatial or pattern recognition questions — all designed to be answerable quickly once you know the underlying approach.

faqs.q: How should I prepare for the time pressure?
faqs.a: Practice enough questions that the common patterns become automatic, and don't get stuck — if a question is taking too long, take your best guess and move on so you don't lose time you need for easier questions later in the set.
